rationale.complete: Round 1 done: dated predictions, synthetic validation at village sampling (size, power, two estimator fixes as amendments), six NE classes, a turn-level erasure test, four period-native tests (#51 personas and NE38, #12 debates, the #44 leader), 32 replication points, post-hoc mechanism checks, scorecard and a dry-run confirmatory script (not run). No holdout run, no second embedding model or alternative style feature set.
rationale.faithfulness: The core claim (style invariant under every natural experiment, carrying no semantic information) is refuted. Style moves at goal switches, across exogenously timed erasures (while content does not), for the Prankster and for #12 judges, and it predicts output as well as content. What holds is narrower: style is a better identity fingerprint than content across goal switches, and a drift-and-reset picture (post hoc) explains the erasure result. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F1 G1 H0 I0.
rationale.usefulness: A cheap, computable identity fingerprint (20 formatting and punctuation rates) that survives task changes better than embeddings: useful for attribution and for detecting model swaps. It comes with actionable warnings: style drifts with context length and resets at context erasure, and assigned registers move it, so monitors must condition on context position and speech act. Not yet validated as a monitor (no ROC, no holdout).

one_line: Style is not conserved: goal switches (T 0.69), forced erasures (0.56, content flat) and assigned registers move it; it identifies agents at 0.76 (content 0.51).

models.note: Strict style conservation refuted; charge plus context-held excitation fits (post hoc)
Style carries as much next-day information as content

v2.claim: Style drifts with context fill and resets at erasure, yet identifies agents better than content
v2.rater: 2 raters (coordinator + blind); log-odds mean credence, mean V

raters.claim: Scope: 32 periods' boundaries (goal switches, erasures, roles). An agent's 20-feature style is not conserved: it moves at goal switches (T_s 0.69, 21/24), at exogenously timed erasures (0.56) and with assigned registers, yet still identifies agents across goal switches better than content (0.76 vs 0.51; chance 0.15).

ladder.factor: replication: goal switches 21/24; style wins identification 22/24
intervention consistent: exogenously timed forced erasures move style
identified: synthetic validation before real data
penalty: style features include topic-adjacent rates (digits, uppercase, colons) that carry the goal-switch shift
penalty: speech act not controlled; content on bge only
